judgments.title: LEE KUAH SHYAN v Lee Kuah Woon & ors
judgments.catchwords: Originating Summons for declaratory relief as to the true construction of the Last Will and Testament - testator’s intention as expressed in the words of the will read as a whole, and not his unexpressed subjective wishes - Second, the court will, so far as the language permits, prefer a construction that gives every clause some operative effect over one that renders any clause meaningless - where two constructions are reasonably open, and one produces an intestacy, be it whole or partial, while the other avoids it, the court prefers the construction that avoids intestacy - the court is not entitled to make a fresh will for the testator merely because it suspects that he did not mean what he plainly said - the court may inform itself of the testator’s actual circumstances at the time he made the will, this includes his family, his property, and his business relationships, to understand what he meant by the words he used, before concluding that those words are ambiguous or deciding how any ambiguity is to be resolved. - company is a legal person distinct from its members, and that a shareholder, even one holding practically the whole of the issued capital, has no legal or equitable proprietary interest in the company’s assets.

judgments.title: WENNIE TAN WEN THENG v TAN BAN KHENG & ors
judgments.catchwords: Facebook posts warning of Cambodian job scam carrying the Plaintiff's photographs carry a defamatory imputation against the Plaintiff. The use of the Plaintiff's pictures is a clear reference to the Plaintiff. No question of publication of the Facebook posts. No reason to disturb finding of fact by Sessions Court Judge that Facebook posts were in fact true and therefore justified. As posts are true, there is no question of malice. Tagging of Facebook posts constitutes re-publication. Mere tagging without comment cannot qualify for fair comment defence. Reynolds privilege defence not available without fulfilling the responsible journalism requirement. Despite posts being justified vis-a-vis the 1st Defendant, the defence of justification not available to 2nd Defendant because it is unpleaded. Damages nominal because the tagging of justified Facebook posts cannot be said to have defamed the Plaintiff further.

judgments.title: LOW ENG HOCK v LOW ENG YEW
judgments.catchwords: CIVIL PROCEDURE: Contempt of court - Leave to commence committal proceedings - Interference with due administration of justice - Contempt not committed in face of court and not founded on breach of court order - Proposed contemnors were plaintiff and company secretary of company whose shares were in dispute - Beneficial ownership of defendant's shares was principal issue at trial - Plaintiff issued notice declaring 100% beneficial ownership after witness testified that plaintiff had never notified any beneficial interest - Company secretary lodged rectification of beneficial ownership record with SSM during trial and before expiry of period given to defendant to respond - Whether conduct capable in law of amounting to contempt - Whether prima facie case of contempt established against each proposed contemnor - Whether timing of impugned acts sufficient to support inference of intention to interfere with administration of justice - Whether statutory notification openly recording a litigant's pleaded case amounted to manufactured or fabricated evidence - Distinction between forged documents and statutory lodgements - Whether non-party company secretary acting under statutory reporting duty could be liable - Whether subpoena by plaintiff made company secretary plaintiff's agent - Whether rule 2B required applicant to serve own notice to show cause before seeking leave - Whether unanswered affidavit averments as to state of mind were to be taken as admitted - Weight of factual matters advanced in submissions without affidavit support - Full and frank disclosure in ex parte application - Whether leave should be refused because matters complained of were for determination at trial and alternative remedies existed - Committal as jurisdiction of last resort - Rules of Court 2012, O 52 mr 2B, 3, 4 - Federal Constitution, art 126 - Courts of Judicature Act 1964, s 13. COMPANY LAW: Beneficial ownership - Register of beneficial owners - Reporting framework - Duty of person who has reason to believe he is beneficial owner to notify company as soon as practicable - Company's notice requiring members to state beneficial ownership - Company secretary's duty to record and lodge changes with Registrar - Whether company or secretary may adjudicate competing claims to beneficial ownership - Whether register is conclusive of beneficial ownership or only prima facie evidence - Whether statutory records must be frozen pending litigation over beneficial ownership - Whether late notification is a matter of regulatory compliance or contempt - Companies Act 2016, Division 8A, ss 60A-60E, 60B(8).
judgments.judge: YA Tuan Kuldeep Kumar a/l Jamna Dass

judgments.title: MOHD ROZI BIN AHMAD & ors v RAMLAH BINTI ZAKARIA
judgments.catchwords: LAND LAW: Indefeasibility of title - FELDA land - Original settler died before individual titles were issued - Administrator of settler's estate later registered as sole proprietor holding 1/1 share without notation of administratorship - Standard FELDA land application form had no field for "Administrator" - Land office practice of registering title in name appearing on application - Original title application file no longer in existence - Whether registration in administrator's sole name was a serious error on the register - Whether the registration amounted to a dealing requiring sanction of court - Whether title was obtained by fraud, misrepresentation, forgery, an insufficient or void instrument, or unlawful acquisition - Whether land registered in sole name of one heir was held on trust for other beneficiaries - Whether rectification of register should be ordered - Effect of more than fifteen years without objection to registration - National Land Code, ss 340, 417. SUCCESSION: Small estates - Distribution - Administrator of settler's estate appointed by Administration Order - Small Estate distribution notes and Form FF recorded apportionment of 66/80 and 14/80 shares to two heirs - Remaining heirs, including first plaintiff, recorded as having renounced their shares on oath - Whether administrator remained a bare administrator holding land for all heirs or became beneficial owner - Whether contemporaneous record of renunciation was effective - Whether administrator acted in breach of fiduciary duty - Whether administrator vested estate property in himself without sanction of court - Whether widow of administrator could be appointed administrator of land as part of his own estate without consent of heirs of original settler - Probate and Administration Act 1959, ss 2, 60. EVIDENCE: Burden of proof - Plaintiffs seeking to impugn registered title - Whether plaintiffs proved error in registration on balance of probabilities - Whether evidential burden shifted to defendant - Credibility - Independent witnesses from FELDA and land office preferred over interested witnesses - Adverse inference - Failure to call FELDA officer who assisted with title application and Estate Officer who conducted small estate proceedings - Failure to produce original title application form - Evidence Act 1950, ss 101-103, 114(g). RESTITUTION: Unjust enrichment - Widow administering lands and retaining their produce - Occasional payments of RM100 by deceased administrator to siblings - Whether payments acknowledged a continuing beneficial entitlement in the plaintiffs - Whether enrichment was at plaintiffs' expense and unjust to retain - Whether a party may take advantage of its own wrong.
judgments.judge: YA Tuan Kuldeep Kumar a/l Jamna Dass

judgments.title: CAMERON ADVENTURES SDN. BHD. v SHUPARSHAD & SONS HOLDINGS SDN. BHD.
judgments.catchwords: CIVIL PROCEDURE: Injunction - Interlocutory mandatory injunction - Application by tenant to be allowed to continue operating business on landlord's land after expiry of fixed-term tenancy pending disposal of suit - Tenancy recorded in consent judgment with express end date - Formal tenancy agreement contemplated by consent judgment never executed - Ex-parte and ad-interim orders granted earlier - Applicable threshold - Whether relief sought was mandatory in substance and effect - Whether relief sought was in substance the final relief sought at trial - Whether plaintiff demonstrated unusually strong and clear case - Whether there was a bona fide serious issue to be tried as to any right of continued occupation - Whether damages were an adequate remedy - Whether plaintiff's own pleaded claim for quantified damages showed that loss was compensable in money - Whether bare undertaking as to damages unsupported by evidence of means was sufficient - Whether balance of convenience favoured registered proprietor - Whether assertions from the bar unsupported by affidavit could be given weight - Whether grant of injunction would preserve or alter status quo - Specific Relief Act 1950, ss 7(2), 53. LANDLORD AND TENANT: Tenancy - Fixed term - Expiry by effluxion of time - Renewal - Consent judgment provided that tenancy would continue until fixed date and that terms of renewal would be agreed three months before expiry - Landlord stated to have no intention to stop tenant's business on expiry unless there was breach - Parties failed to agree terms of renewal - Rent calculated as percentage of revenue collected - Landlord insisted on minimum monthly rent not provided for in consent judgment - Whether statement of intention conferred enforceable right to remain in occupation - Whether renewal clause was an unenforceable agreement to agree - Whether fixed revenue-sharing ratio alone was sufficient to constitute a renewed tenancy - Whether turnover-based rent converted tenancy into joint venture - Whether landlord precluded from relying on absence of renewal on ground that it was self-induced - Whether landlord could recover possession otherwise than by court proceedings. CONTRACT: Consent judgment - Construction - Express term that arrangement was not to be construed as a joint venture - Whether party could disregard express term and contend that relationship was in substance a joint venture - Whether factual matrix and prior negotiations admissible to contradict express terms or imply a right of renewal - Whether there was consensus ad idem on terms of renewed tenancy - Whether principle that no man may take advantage of his own wrong applied where tenancy ended on agreed date.
judgments.judge: YA Tuan Kuldeep Kumar a/l Jamna Dass

judgments.catchwords: Offence under section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 read together with section 34 of the Penal Code - Whether the trial judge should have informed at the close of the prosecution's case, that the defence was being called upon to answer a case of actual trafficking or presumed trafficking? - Overwhelming evidence proved the elements of custody, control, and knowledge - Actual possession of the impugned drugs was established - Section 180 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Code - Procedure after conclusion of case for prosecution - No statutory or legal requirement to state the presumption when calling for the defence - Formal verbal label for an evidentiary rule at the close of the prosecution's case is unnecessary - Statutory presumption of trafficking under section 37(da)(xvi) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 - Section 422 of the Criminal Procedure Code - Not vitiate the conviction - No miscarriage of justice - Failure either to make or to record such a finding does not ipso facto - The law does not require a mini-judgment or detailed legal reasons at the close of the prosecution’s case
